signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Escalation
signals.text: NZD COT LF short -23.0k (pctl 4) contrasts with JPY outperformance as escalating Strait of Hormuz conflict spurs haven demand into the open. JPY leads the G10 scorecard with a +2.298% 1W average while NZD lags at -1.445% across G10 pairs, generating a 3.742% bilateral divergence that overrides the 175bp nominal carry disadvantage. The BoJ policy meeting on 18 Sep determines whether domestic rate hike expectations provide additional tailwinds to JPY strength. Trade bias: Short NZD/JPY into the Sydney/Tokyo open. Catalyst: Escalation headlines in the Strait of Hormuz and the BoJ meeting on 18 Sep. Risk: Reversal of Middle East geopolitical tensions pushes risk sentiment higher, triggering a rebound toward the BEER fair value of 94.28.

signals.title: USD/JPY — BoJ Hawk Rhetoric vs OIS Carry Advantage
signals.text: JPY COT LF net short of -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18) leaves the market vulnerable to sharp short-covering after Friday's close at 156.22. Hawkish commentary from BoJ members ahead of their 2027 term expirations reinforces JPY demand, even though the +268bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential heavily favors the dollar. The BoJ meeting on 18 Sep resolves whether rate hike momentum forces leveraged funds to accelerate position liquidations. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY targeting a test below the 200-day SMA at 158.45. Catalyst: BoJ meeting on 18 Sep and Middle East geopolitical developments. Risk: Widening yield spreads via a continued US bond sell-off above 4.80% invalidates the short-squeeze thesis.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Speculative Long Unwind Risk
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +50,250 contracts (pctl 94, 73.5% long) creates acute unwinding risk following Friday's close at 0.7205. Extreme retail positioning of 90% short diverges sharply from leveraged longs, while credit spread widening from the US Treasury sell-off threatens risk-sensitive high-beta currencies. The RBA meeting on 29 Sep determines whether the +69bp AONIA-SOFR carry cushion can withstand a broader shift into defensive assets. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD toward the 20-day SMA at 0.7135. Catalyst: Monday open risk sentiment following Persian Gulf naval tensions. Risk: Continued commodity index rally driven by crude oil supply constraints pushes AUD/USD above 0.7250.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Rate Decision vs Speculative Short Saturation
signals.text: EUR COT LF short -52,784 contracts (pctl 4, z -2.15) limits additional downside momentum after Friday's close at 1.1621. August US non-farm payrolls beat expectations and reinforced Fed rate hike expectations, but the ECB meeting on 10 Sep introduces hike risk that challenges the +147bp SOFR-ESTR carry advantage held by the dollar. The ECB policy rate decision on 10 Sep determines whether monetary tightening narrows the EUR/USD policy differential. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD on short-covering into policy divergence risk. Catalyst: ECB policy meeting on 10 Sep. Risk: Fed hike pricing accelerates following US CPI release, driving EUR/USD below the 50-day SMA support at 1.1512.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Crowded Leveraged Longs Facing BoE Policy Inertia
signals.text: GBP COT LF long +47,504 contracts (pctl 93, 71.6% long) exposes the pair to liquidation pressure after Friday's close at 1.3517. With BoE policy on hold at 3.75% and UK ESI registering -6.7, stagnant British growth contrasts with resilient US employment and an elevated GBP option volatility risk premium (VRP +6.3%). The BoE meeting on 17 Sep serves as the primary gauge for whether UK monetary policy can defend the neutral carry posture. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD targeting the 50-day SMA at 1.3456. Catalyst: UK GDP data and the BoE meeting on 17 Sep. Risk: Sustained progress on US-Russia peace talks eases global risk aversion and supports sterling above 1.3555.
